name: Frame Locked Intro SFX And Drums
use_when: A premium intro uses fast text, logo, flicker, underline, or camera movement that needs sonic weight.
The intro should feel high-energy without burying the proof quote or body handoff.
A reusable brand or series bumper needs consistent sound grammar.
avoid_when: The intro is serious, quiet, or trust-led and SFX would make it feel cheap.
The sound cue does not match an actual visible event.
Dialogue, quote proof, or the first body line becomes harder to understand.
The intro already has enough motion and sound would add clutter.

timeline_pattern.pattern: music_pulse -> logo_hit -> text_flicker_pops -> underline_or_keyword_hit -> short_tail_or_fade -> body_audio
timeline_pattern.sync_rule: Place every SFX exactly on the visible frame it sells: logo reveal, text pop, flicker, cut, beat drop, underline, or transition.
timeline_pattern.music_rule: A fast drum or 120 BPM-style pulse can support intro pace, but it should not dictate unrelated cuts.
timeline_pattern.handoff_rule: Fade, duck, or cut the intro bed so the first body line starts cleanly.
timeline_pattern.silence_rule: Remove any SFX cue that does not align to screen action.

motion.rule: Sound accents should be driven by visible motion markers, not by decoration.

sound.rule: Use short, varied, frame-accurate hits/pops/whooshes and keep speech or proof audio dominant.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: Land intro hits within 0-1 frames of the visible event for a premium feel.
keyframe_values.bpm_start: Try music around 120 BPM for fast intro packaging, then adjust to the brand and speaker pace.
keyframe_values.handoff_fade: Use a quick fade or duck over the final 4-12 frames when the body speech starts immediately.

captions.rule: Do not pair loud hits with dense caption motion unless the intro is intentionally high-energy and speech stays clear.

color.rule: No direct color rule; avoid flash/SFX combinations that hide brand or proof text.

implementation.ffmpeg: Place SFX with sample/frame-accurate offsets, use atrim/adelay/amix/volume/afade, and render a short waveform review around the intro handoff.
implementation.remotion: Trigger SFX from the same frame constants as logo, flicker, underline, and camera moves; store bpm, eventFrame, gain, and fadeOutFrames.
implementation.blender: Use timeline markers for logo/text/camera events and align audio strips to those markers.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add beat markers, place short SFX on visible text/logo events, trim tails, and preview on phone speakers.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers for every visible intro event, place SFX clips on separate tracks, adjust clip gain, and duck/fade the intro bed before body dialogue.

common_mistakes: Adding SFX that do not match what happens onscreen.
Letting the intro beat overpower the social proof quote.
Using a beat grid to force cuts that do not support brand, proof, or outcome.
Leaving the intro bed too loud under the first body line.
Using the same hit on every text flicker until the intro sounds pasted together.
qc: Does every SFX cue land on a visible intro event?
Do logo, text, flicker, underline, and transition hits land within 0-1 frames when precision matters?
Is the proof quote or body speech intelligible under the intro bed?
Does the intro music hand off cleanly to the main content?
Are repeated hits varied or low enough that they do not feel mechanical?
